lines: 16-step sequencer with seven programmable rows per step, per-step probability and ratchets, ten traversal orders and a clock divider and multiplier
Sets the semitone for that step, 0 to 11, or 0 to 23 when the two-octave pitch range is chosen on the menu
Shifts that step by whole octaves, -2 to +2
Cycles that step through the eight step modes: Play, Mute, Skip, Accum Up, Accum Down, Pulse, Gated and Hold
Sets the gate length of that step as a fraction of one sequence period, 1% to 95%, with no effect while the module is in TRIG mode
Sets the voltage that step puts out on the first modulation output, 0 to 10 over whatever range the menu gives that output
Sets the voltage that step puts out on the second modulation output, 0 to 10 over whatever range the menu gives that output
Left of centre this is the chance that step plays, 100% down to 0%; right of centre it is a ratchet count of 2 to 8, read only by the Pulse, Gated and Hold modes
Sets how many steps the active window holds, 1 to 16
Sets which physical step the active window starts at; the window wraps past step 16 back to step 1
Picks the traversal order: Pendulum, Backward, Forward, Random, Drunk, Ping-Pong, Odd/Even, Jump, Converge or Diverge
Switches the gate output between gates whose length follows each step's duration and fixed 10ms triggers
Divides or multiplies the incoming clock, from divide by 48 to multiply by 48, before swing is applied
Delays every other sequence tick, 0% to 60%, after the ratio has been applied
Slews the pitch output between steps, 0 to 2 seconds; gates, modulation and step selection are not delayed
Sets how many semitones an Accum Up or Accum Down step adds to or takes from its own stored offset, 0 to 24
Sets the range the per-step accumulator wraps through, 1 to 12 semitones either side of zero; at OFF it wraps through the full -12 to +12 semitones
Scales the chance of every step playing, 0% to 100%, multiplied with each step's own probability
Randomises all sixteen values of that row at once; double-click to set the row back to its default instead
Lowers every value of that row inside the active window by one step of that row's own grid, stopping at the row's limit
Raises every value of that row inside the active window by one step of that row's own grid, stopping at the row's limit
The clock the sequencer runs on; a rising edge above 1V advances one sequence tick, subject to the ratio and swing
A rising edge above 1V returns to the first step of the active window, clears every step's accumulator and interrupts a held or ratcheted gate
A rising edge above 1V randomises all sixteen values of that row, whether or not they are inside the active window
Transposes the pitch output at a volt per octave, quantised to semitones and limited to four octaves either way
The pitch of the selected step: its semitone and octave, plus transpose, plus that step's accumulated offset, with the glide applied
A 10V gate or trigger for the selected step, its length set by that step's duration knob and the gate mode switch
One 10V gate per position of the active window, on a polyphonic cable whose first channel is the window's first position rather than physical step 1
A 10V, 10ms pulse when the traversal completes a cycle; Random never produces one, and Pendulum produces one at each turn
The first modulation lane's voltage for the selected step
The second modulation lane's voltage for the selected step
Note — nothing moves until a clock is patched; there is no internal tempo, and with the clock jack empty the gate, poly and end-of-cycle outputs stop while pitch and modulation hold.
Note — Skip steps are bypassed without taking any time in Forward, Backward, Pendulum, Random and Drunk; in the other five orders they keep their place in the order and are played silently.
Note — a ratio other than one to one needs the clock period measured first, so allow an edge or two after patching or changing the clock source.
Note — the fractional multipliers of one and a half and two and a half re-anchor on every incoming edge and come out close to one to one and two to one; use the whole-number ones instead.
Note — a failed probability test blocks the accumulation as well as the gate, and pitch and modulation update to the selected step either way.
Menu — EOC on reset — off by default, makes the reset input produce an end-of-cycle pulse as well
Menu — Direction mode — picks the traversal order, the same setting as the knob on the panel
Menu — Jump stride — how many positions the Jump order moves each advance, from two to seven
Menu — Pitch range: 1 octave (0..11), 2 octaves (0..23) — sets what the pitch knobs cover, rescaling the values already entered
Menu — Range Mod 1 — sets the voltage range of the first modulation output, from ±10V down to 0V..1V
Menu — Range Mod 2 — sets the voltage range of the second modulation output, from ±10V down to 0V..1V

lines: MIDI to CV interface for note, controller, clock and transport messages, with eight assignable controller outputs
Pitch of the current note at a volt per octave, MIDI note 60 giving 0V, with the global pitch bend added; one, four or eight channels depending on the play mode
10V while a note is held and 0V otherwise, with one channel per voice or per tracked MIDI channel
The note's MIDI velocity mapped from 0 to 127 onto 0 to 10V, held after the gate falls
The value of that output's assigned controller number, 0 to 127 mapped onto 0 to 10V
A 10V, 1ms pulse for every incoming MIDI clock tick, which is 24 of them to the quarter note
A 10V, 1ms pulse every so many MIDI clock ticks, the count set on the menu and starting at 24, which gives one pulse to the quarter note
10V after a MIDI start or continue message and 0V after a stop
Note — nothing comes out until a MIDI driver and device are chosen in the module's menu; the display shows the play mode and the MIDI channel being received.
Note — a note-on at velocity zero is treated as a note-off, controller 123 lowers every gate, and a MIDI stop lowers every gate and takes the run output low.
Note — Multitrack and Matriceal read one note per MIDI channel and switch the input to Omni when they are chosen; check that Omni is set after loading a patch.
Menu — Play Mode: Mono, Poly, Chord, Multitrack, Matriceal — sets how incoming notes are spread across the voice outputs and how many channels they carry
Menu — Chord: unison gate — in Chord mode, makes all eight gate channels go high while any voice is playing rather than each gating on its own
Menu — Pitch Bend Range — how far a full pitch bend moves the pitch outputs, one to twelve semitones, starting at two
Menu — CLK/n Division — how many MIDI clock ticks pass between pulses on the divided clock output: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 24
Menu — CC Assignments — one submenu per controller output, choosing which of the 128 MIDI controller numbers it follows; number 123 is kept for all-notes-off and produces no voltage

OxiCv.notes: ONE has no parameters and no inputs, so the only things to click for help are its jacks. Its MULTI expander goes immediately to the right. The eight controller outputs are assigned by controller number rather than per MIDI channel, so any matching message that passes the Rack MIDI filter updates them.

lines: Expander for ONE that gives eight MIDI channels their own pitch, gate and velocity jacks; it goes immediately to the right of ONE
Picks which of the sixteen MIDI channels that row follows, stepped to whole channel numbers
The current note on that row's MIDI channel, at a volt per octave with ONE's global pitch bend added
10V while that row's channel has a note held, and 0V otherwise
The velocity of that row's current note, 0 to 127 mapped onto 0 to 10V
Note — with no ONE immediately to the left, every output here stays at 0V.
Note — each MIDI channel holds one note at a time, so a new note on that channel replaces the one before it; two rows may watch the same channel if a duplicate is wanted.
Note — the arrangement the maker supports is ONE set to Multitrack or Matriceal with its MIDI input set to Omni, so that every channel these rows select reaches it.

lines: Turns the knobs and faders of an Akai APC40 into CV, on a fixed controller map with no learning and no remapping
Scales that output from -1 through zero to +1, so a fully anticlockwise setting gives 0 to -10V and the centre holds the output at 0V
One of the eight track controls, its own controller number on MIDI channel 1 mapped onto 0 to 10V before the attenuverter above it
One of the eight device controls, its own controller number on MIDI channel 1 mapped onto 0 to 10V before the attenuverter above it
The cue level control, controller 47 on MIDI channel 1, mapped onto 0 to 10V before its attenuverter
The master control, controller 14 on MIDI channel 1, mapped onto 0 to 10V before its attenuverter
The crossfader, controller 11 on MIDI channel 1, mapped onto 0 to 10V before its attenuverter
One of the eight channel faders, controller 7 on its own MIDI channel, mapped straight onto 0 to 10V with no attenuverter in the way
Note — choose the hardware's MIDI port in the module's menu; MIDI reception is forced to Omni because the eight faders share one controller number across eight channels.
Note — only control change messages are read, and nothing is sent back to the hardware, so motorised faders and knob rings are not updated.
Note — an attenuverter multiplies rather than offsets, so at any setting a controller value of zero comes out as 0V.

lines: Ducking VCA: every trigger drops the gain fast, holds it down and brings it back, with an envelope and end-of-cycle output of its own
Sets how long the gain takes to come back, 40ms to 1 second, on an exponential scale that spreads the short times out
Sets how far the gain falls at the bottom of a duck, 0% for no ducking at all and 100% for silence
Sets how much each hit varies from the last, 0% to 100%, as a random walk over recovery time, depth and curve rather than unrelated noise on each hit
Sets the gain ceiling the audio rests at, 0% to 100%; it scales the audio at rest as well as during a duck
Fires a duck on every current envelope channel without a trigger patched; it acts on the press rather than repeating while held
A rising edge above 1V starts a duck, and the signal has to fall below 0.1V before another can fire, so a held gate ducks once; how many channels are patched here sets the envelope polyphony
Adds to the depth knob, 10V for 100 percentage points, sampled at the moment the channel triggers
Left or mono audio in
Right audio in; with this jack empty the left input feeds the right path as well
Scales the gain the level knob sets, 0V closing the VCA and 10V passing the full ceiling; with nothing patched it takes nothing away
The ducking gain as a control voltage: 10V at rest, dipping on each trigger and recovering
The left audio at the ducked gain; with no audio patched this output carries no channels
The right audio at the ducked gain; with no audio patched this output carries no channels
A 10V, 1ms pulse when a recovery reaches its natural end; a trigger arriving before that cancels the pulse for that cycle
Note — each duck is a fixed 2ms fall and a 12ms hold before the recovery starts, and a new trigger during a cycle starts a fresh fall from wherever the gain has reached.
Note — the bar behind the level slider shows the gain being applied rather than the audio, so it moves with the duck even in silence; the white marker is the ceiling the slider sets.
Note — with no audio patched the module works as an envelope generator, and patching the end-of-cycle output back into the trigger jack makes it cycle on its own.
Menu — Recovery curve: Exponential, Linear, Logarithmic — the shape the gain takes coming back from a duck
Menu — Freeze jitter — stops the random walks advancing, so every hit reuses the current variation
Menu — Per-channel envelopes — gives each polyphonic channel its own envelope and jitter, instead of one envelope shared by all of them
Menu — Level attenuates ENV — makes the level control scale the envelope output as well as the audio, including its resting voltage
Menu — Reset jitter seed — draws a new random seed and restarts every channel's random walk, without firing an envelope

SideChain.notes: Two jacks carry no label on the panel: the one under DEPTH is the depth CV and the one under the level slider is the VCA CV, each tied to its control by a hairline. The VCA input was added in 2.5.7, after the manual was written, and the manual read here (Manuals/CAP_Manual_EN.md at this commit) does describe it. lines: Generative sequencer that scatters a cloud of points from a seed, joins the ones a set distance apart, and walks that network on each clock to make pitch, gates, accents and two modulation voltages
Sets the number the cloud of points is generated from, 0 to 999; the same number rebuilds the same cloud
Sets how many points the cloud holds, 8 to 64
Sets the distance at which two points count as joined, 0.25 to 2
Widens or narrows the margin around that distance, 0.01 to 0.2, as the fine adjustment to the radius
Thins or fills the connections in the network, 0% to 100%
Picks how the walker moves: to the next neighbour, to a neighbour chosen by a repeatable pseudo-random rule, or to whichever neighbour has the most connections of its own
Sets how many octaves the pitch output spreads the points across, 1 to 4
Sets the gate length, 5% to 95% of the clock period
Sets how often a step produces a gate at all, 15% to 100%, with the walker moving on either way
Freezes the phrase into a repeating loop: to the right a 16-step loop and to the left a 32-step loop, further from the centre freezing more of the steps
The clock the walker moves on; each rising edge takes it to another point, and with this jack empty nothing advances
A rising edge returns the walk to its starting state, so a phrase can repeat from the same place
Adds to the seed knob, a hundred seeds per volt, which rebuilds the whole cloud; slow or stepped voltages suit it, audio rate does not
Adds to the density knob, a tenth of its travel per volt
The pitch of the current point, taken from its horizontal position and quantised to C minor
A 10V gate when the current point produces one, its length set by the gate length knob
An accent voltage from 0 to 10V, higher for a point with more connections of its own
A 0 to 10V reading of the current point's horizontal position, the same figure the pitch is made from
A 0 to 10V reading of the current point's vertical position, as a second modulation source
Note — the display draws the network as it stands: points, the lines joining them, and the current point in fuchsia, drawn larger for a longer gate and brighter for a higher gate density.
Note — the module is deterministic: the same seed and the same knob positions rebuild the same network and the same phrase.
Menu — Poly seed mode: Shared seed, Per-voice seed — whether the extra polyphonic voices offset one cloud or each build a cloud of their own
Menu — Poly voices — how many channels every output carries, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8

lines: Monophonic acid voice after the TB-303: oscillator, resonant lowpass filter, decay envelope, accent, slide and output stage, with a CV jack and attenuverter for each main control
Sets the reference tuning of the oscillator, 400Hz to 480Hz, separately from the pitch input
Sets the filter cutoff, about 314Hz to 2394Hz, on an exponential scale
Sets the filter resonance, 0% to 100%
Sets how far the decay envelope sweeps the filter, 0% to 100%, on a curve that puts most of the movement in the upper part of the travel until the taper is made linear on the menu
Sets the envelope decay on a logarithmic scale, 200ms to 2.5 seconds in the circuit model or about 460ms to 4.6 seconds in the Open303 model; an accented note uses the shortest time of that range
Sets how strongly an accented note is emphasised, 0% to 100%
Picks the oscillator waveform, sawtooth or square
Sets how much of the jack below it reaches the control above it: centre for none, clockwise for positive and anticlockwise for inverted, with ±5V covering the whole control at full depth
Pitch at a volt per octave, 0V giving C4; it is continuous unless the menu quantises it to semitones
Starts and ends notes, going high at 1V and staying high until it falls below 0.1V
Marks the note beginning as accented while it is at 1V or above, which changes loudness, filter movement and the accent envelope; the red lamp follows it

Requests a legato transition into the next note, on the same 1V and 0.1V thresholds as the gate; a gate falling while this is high keeps the voice alive for the next note, and the blue lamp follows it
A voltage modulating the control above it, at the depth and polarity its attenuverter sets
The voice output at a fixed full level, with no level control on the panel; it is clamped at ±12V, and accent and saturation can make it far hotter than an unaccented note
Note — an ATEK303 SEQ placed immediately to the left sends pitch, gate, accent and slide without cables; a cable in any of those four jacks replaces that one signal only.
Note — each modulation jack starts with its attenuverter at the centre, so patching a cable does nothing until the small knob beside it is turned.
Menu — Sound model: Circuit (ATEK), Open303 original — picks a whole group of oscillator, filter, decay, saturation and slide settings at once; Custom shows when they match neither
Menu — Motor — under Fine tuning, picks the oscillator, either Open303's wavetables or the model taken from the schematic
Menu — Pulse width (TM5) — under Fine tuning, the width of the square wave, 44% through 56%
Menu — Square droop — under Fine tuning, how far the square wave tilts across each cycle, from none to 60Hz
Menu — Saw: reset corner — under Fine tuning, how hard the sawtooth's reset is, 1 microsecond sharp through 20 microseconds round
Menu — Saw droop — under Fine tuning, how far the sawtooth tilts, 0.7Hz through 15Hz
Menu — Motor — under Fine tuning, picks the filter, either Open303's or a diode ladder model
Menu — Linear resonance (VR4 linear pot) — under Fine tuning, makes the resonance knob follow the circuit's linear law rather than Open303's curve
Menu — Drive — under Fine tuning, how hard the signal hits the filter, 0dB, 6dB or 12dB
Menu — Decay range — under Fine tuning, what the decay knob covers, Open303's 460ms to 4.6 seconds or the circuit's 200ms to 2.5 seconds
Menu — Accent accumulation (C72 network) — under Fine tuning, lets closely spaced accents build on each other and carry into the notes that follow
Menu — Accent stages — under Fine tuning, which accent envelopes are used: the fast 100ms one, the slow 450ms one, or both as the circuit has them
Menu — Log Env Mod taper (VR5 audio pot) — under Fine tuning, gives the envelope amount knob an audio taper; turning it off makes the knob and its CV linear
Menu — Slide in semitones/s (as the circuit) — under Fine tuning, glides in pitch rather than in frequency, which keeps the rate even across the range
Menu — Slide τ — under Fine tuning, the time constant of the glide, 60ms, 120ms or 220ms
Menu — Quantize pitch to semitones — under Fine tuning, rounds the incoming pitch to chromatic semitones
Menu — Limit to the 303 range (C1–C4) — under Fine tuning, clamps the note range to the original three octaves; without quantisation a fractional semitone can carry slightly past those bounds
Menu — Auto-legato (slide without SLIDE input) — under Fine tuning, starts a glide when the pitch changes under a held gate; off by default, so a moving CV does not glide by accident
Menu — OTA saturation (BA662A, before the VCA) — under Fine tuning, None, Soft or Hard saturation ahead of the amplifier
Menu — Output saturation (mixer + LA4140) — under Fine tuning, None, Soft or Hard saturation in the final output path
Menu — Analogue drift (R-2R DAC + posistor) — under Fine tuning, how much the tuning and cutoff wander: None, Subtle, Marked or Heavy, the menu giving the cents and per cent for each
Menu — Unit (DAC error pattern) — under Fine tuning, picks one of four repeatable note-by-note tuning error patterns, which does not change from note to note

lines: Acid pattern generator: a seed and a handful of musical controls make a repeatable pattern of notes, rests, ties, accents and slides, which mutation buttons then vary
Makes a new pattern from a new seed, or mutates all three layers of the current one while BLOCK is lit
Sets how many steps the loop plays before it wraps, 1 to 64, taking effect at once without regenerating anything
Sets the gate length of an ordinary note, 5% to 100% of the measured clock period, with a small gap kept before the next edge
Sets how much of a new pattern is notes rather than rests, 5% to 100%; it shapes the next generation rather than the pattern playing now
Sets how widely a new pattern spreads in pitch and octave, 0% to 100%; it shapes the next generation rather than the pattern playing now
Sets how much of a new pattern is accented, 0% to 100%; it shapes the next generation rather than the pattern playing now
Sets how much of a new pattern slides, 0% to 100%; a slide is kept only between adjacent notes of different pitch
Transposes playback to one of the twelve chromatic roots, at once and without regenerating the pattern
Picks the scale the pattern is read through: Acid minor pentatonic, Natural minor, Phrygian, Harmonic minor, Dorian, Blues, Major or Chromatic; changing it moves the notes that are playing now
Locks the seed, so that generating mutates the pattern instead of replacing it; the lamp and the menu's Lock seed are the same setting
Runs two mutation operations on the rest, note and tie layer, which can move an attack or change a note into a tie
Runs two mutation operations on the pitch family, which in this version moves notes between octaves
Runs three mutation operations on the accents and slides
Swaps the generation controls for the pattern editor in the same panel space, leaving the step lamps, jacks and mutation buttons where they are
The clock the pattern plays on; each rising edge advances one step, and there is no internal clock
A rising edge prepares step 1, which the next clock edge then plays; it does not change the pattern or the seed
A rising edge does what the generate button does: a new seed, or a mutation of all three layers while BLOCK is lit
Pitch of the current step at a volt per octave, the scale degree plus the root and the base octave; during a rest it holds the previous pitch
10V while the current note sounds, its length set by the gate knob, held through a tie and, if the menu says so, across a slide
10V on an accented note, or a held velocity-style level when the menu switches this output to velocity
10V on a note that slides into the next one, and low for rests, ties and transitions that cannot form a slide
A 10V, 1ms pulse at step 1, including the very first clock edge after a reset or a patch load
Note — an external clock is required; pressing generate changes the pattern but does not advance it, and the first clock edge starts step 1.
Note — the sixteen lamps show the pattern: dark for a rest, green for an attack, blue for a tie, amber for a note that slides, red for an accent, and bright red on the step being played.
Note — an ATEK303 placed immediately to the right receives pitch, gate, accent and slide without cables, and the sequencer's own glide switches off so that the voice performs the slide.
Note — the editor's piano roll, its octave, gate, accent and slide rows and its page strip are drawn widgets rather than controls, so clicking them edits the pattern and cannot bring up help.
Menu — Lock seed — the same setting as the BLOCK button on the panel
Menu — Mutation scope: Current page (16 steps), Whole pattern (64 steps) — how much of the pattern the mutation buttons act on
Menu — Mutate time (2 operations) — the same action as the MUT TIME button
Menu — Mutate pitches / octaves (2 operations) — the same action as the MUT NOTE/OCT button
Menu — Mutate accents / slides (3 operations) — the same action as the MUT SLD/ACC button
Menu — Undo last mutation — puts back the pattern as it was before the last mutation; there is one level of it, and generating with a new seed clears it
Menu — Clear pattern — empties the pattern for drawing one in the editor, keeping the seed and leaving a note on step 1; it takes the undo slot, so it can be undone
Menu — Load MIDI file… — reads a standard MIDI file on a sixteenth-note grid and replaces the pattern with it, keeping the lowest note of any chord
Menu — Bar — appears once a loaded file runs past 16 steps, and moves between the file's bars without opening it again
Menu — Forget file — drops the reference to the loaded file; the pattern that came from it carries on playing
Menu — Gate held through slides (legato) — keeps the gate high across a slide instead of leaving a short gap for the next attack
Menu — Own glide on the V/Oct output (disables itself when ATEK303 is attached) — glides the pitch output after a slide, at a rate proportional to the clock
Menu — Base octave: C1 (-3), C2 (-2), C3 (-1), C4 (0), C5 (+1) — the octave the pattern is read in, which starts at C2
Menu — Accent as velocity CV — turns the accent output from a 10V gate into held velocity-style levels
Menu — Accent level: 10 V, 8 V, or 5 V — the voltage an accented note holds in velocity mode
Menu — Base level (unaccented note) — the voltage an unaccented note holds in velocity mode, 0V, 1V, 2V or 3V

0.why: clock and trigger detection uses Schmitt thresholds around 0.1V and 1V, per the manual's CLOCK section

1.why: the same trigger detection as the clock, per the manual's RESET section

2.why: the same trigger detection as the clock, per the manual's GEN section

0.why: monophonic pitch, the scale degree plus root and base octave, per the manual's V/OCT section

1.why: 10V while the note is active, per the manual's GATE section

4.why: a 10V, 1ms pulse at step 1, per the manual's EOC section

ATEK303SEQ.notes: The installed build takes STEPS from 1 to 64 (Atek303Seq.cpp:132 with ACID_MAX_STEPS 64 in AcidGen.hpp:43) and carries a Mutation scope menu item; the manual at this commit is written for 2.5.5 and says 1 to 16 steps with no mutation scope. The pattern editor, the four page lamps, the sixteen step lamps and the acid sticker that generates are all drawn widgets rather than parameters, so none of them can be clicked for help.
